_doc: Editorial config for the data tables on /benchmarks/. The engine-comparison table pulls its numeric values from scalability_results.json (the raw bench output); this file supplies display labels, captions, and the scenario picker's commentary. Speed-cell templates: {throughput}, {mp}, {memory} are substituted from the matching engine's row at the showcase MP. Each table may carry an optional column_sizing block to override the default first-column auto-sizing rule (see _column_sizing_doc below). Rows whose measurements have not been taken yet are handled by the provisional convention (see _provisional_doc below).
_column_sizing_doc: Default first-column auto-sizing rule used by both tables. The renderer measures each first-column cell at single-line max-content width; if that width exceeds threshold_ratio × the resulting other-column width, the first column is capped at cap_ratio × the other-column width and its cells wrap. Override per-table by placing a `column_sizing` block inside engine_table or scenario_table.
_provisional_doc: A bench row may carry "provisional": true with its measured fields null. The renderer marks every engine whose rows are all provisional with `marker` beside the label, and un-hides the matching [data-bench-note] paragraph under the table, filled with `text`. Both are driven off the data, so dropping the flag and the null values in scalability_results.json clears the marker and hides the note with no edit here or in the markup.

provisional_note.text: † PMTiles measurements are pending. PMTiles is not a fourth engine: it is the MapReduce engine writing one indexed .pmtiles archive instead of a tile tree, so the row shares its grid, its tile count and its compute path. libviprs-bench has no storage axis until libviprs#993 lands, and a guessed number on a benchmarks page is a number somebody quotes back, so these cells stay empty until that run publishes. The five figures above come from the same run and get their PMTiles series then.

engine_table._showcase_mp_target_doc: Renders the bench row whose megapixel count is closest to this target. Anchors the showcase numbers to the size the surrounding prose discusses, so the table doesn't drift onto a larger benchmarked size whenever the bench grid grows. Update both this value and the prose in benchmarks.html together if you want a different size.
